task.title: Shopping receipt
task.description: The platform sets the order data: price (number), quantityText (a string, as from a form) and discountPercent (number). Declare with const: quantity - the quantity as a number via Number(); subtotal - price × quantity; discount - the discount in so'm (discountPercent per cent of subtotal); total - the amount to pay; isExpensive - true if total is greater than 100000; receipt - the string "Total: <total> UZS" built with a template string. Print receipt to the console. The code is checked on several data sets, so do not write ready-made numbers.

tests.name: quantity is the number 3
tests.fail: quantityText is a string. Convert it: const quantity = Number(quantityText);

tests.name: The quantity is converted with Number(quantityText)
discount = 13500
tests.fail: The discount in so'm: subtotal * discountPercent / 100.

tests.name: isExpensive is the boolean true
tests.fail: isExpensive = total > 100000; - a comparison is already true or false.

tests.name: receipt equals "Total: 121500 UZS"
tests.fail: Check the text: Total, colon, space, number, space, UZS.

tests.name: receipt is built with a template string containing ${total}
The receipt is printed to the console
Another order: 20000 × "7" with a 5% discount = 133000
tests.fail: The result is wrong on other data: do not write ready numbers, calculate through the variables.

tests.name: Exactly 100000 is not greater than 100000
The program runs without errors
tests.fail: There is an error in the code - read its text in the console.

hints: Percent of a number: subtotal * discountPercent / 100.
A comparison already gives true or false: const isExpensive = total > 100000;
A template string uses backticks: `Total: ${total} UZS`.
The platform runs the code on several orders - a written-in 121500 only works for the first one.

questions.question: What does typeof "42" return?
questions.explanation: A value in quotes is a string, even if it contains digits.

questions.question: What does console.log("5" + 3); print?
questions.explanation: + with a string joins: the result is the string "53".

questions.question: Which values have the type number?
questions.explanation: NaN is a special value of type number; "10" is a string.

questions.question: Match the value with its type.
How do you correctly get a number from quantityText = "4"?
questions.explanation: Number() converts a string to a number; + 0 would join into "40".

questions.question: What does this print: const name = "Timur"; console.log(`Hello, ${name}!`);
questions.explanation: Inside backticks ${...} is replaced with the value.

questions.question: Which expressions give true?
questions.explanation: === compares value and type: the number 5 is not equal to the string "5".

questions.question: Which property returns the number of characters in a string? Type the property name.
What does this print: let s = " yes "; s.trim(); console.log(s.length);
questions.explanation: trim() returns a new string, s did not change: it has 5 characters.

questions.question: Match the expression with the result when let n = 10.
questions.explanation: += adds, - subtracts, % is the remainder, ** is the exponent.

questions.question: What does Number("12px") return?
questions.explanation: The string is not made only of digits - the conversion fails and the result is NaN.
